props.title: Two apps, two sets of tab IDs
props.deck: The old plugin was working, but it was talking to a different runtime.

left.label: Before: daemon-only
left.body: `src/herdr.ts` asks `herdr api snapshot` for daemon IDs, then sends `herdr tab rename`. A native `tb…` ID returns `tab_not_found`.

right.label: After: native backend
right.body: `src/herdr-app.ts` reads app topology and core facts. The naming service writes through `herdr-app do tab.rename` with the selected native ID.

props.caption: One naming policy, with a native read path and native write path. The model suggests text; the service decides whether to use it.

beats.text: **Read the right world.** The native client combines app topology, focus and a read-only core document. It collects context from the selected tab only.
**Reuse the policy.** The existing naming service asks the selected provider for a candidate. The live test used localhost, not a real provider account.
**Check again.** After inference, the service rechecks manual ownership and source identity. A changed tab or program invalidates the result.
**Write through the app.** Only the selected local native tab can change. Spaces, panes and unrelated tabs remain outside the write scope.

props.summary: Why OSC titles and Luau mods were not the fix

props.content:
The current `herdr-t3` layout displays a meaningful terminal title for an unnamed tab. An explicit tab name wins. The stock layout differs, so emitting OSC 0/2 is not a dependable tab-naming API.

Sheprd's Luau mods and automations belong to the other app. Native mods are JavaScript, but this implementation needs no mod or layout edits.

props.title: Your later edit wins
props.deck: The live test held the provider response, changed the name, then released the outdated result.
props.takeaway: A candidate is not permission to overwrite a newer choice.

props.alt: Native tab displaying Keep My Manual Title after a delayed response was discarded
props.caption: The delayed model result did not replace Keep My Manual Title.

rows.title: Numeric manual names remain manual
rows.body: The live tab named `123` made no provider request during ordinary naming. Raw core names remove the ambiguity of displayed tab numbers.

rows.title: Only the selected tab changes
rows.body: Native writes reject daemon IDs, remote spaces, pane targets and unrelated tabs. The live test compared every other tab name before and after.

rows.title: Changed sources invalidate inference
rows.body: Contained tests cover closed tabs, changed sessions and replaced foreground programs. The service discards their pending results.

rows.title: Provider failure leaves the label alone
rows.body: Invalid local provider output returned exit 1 with no rename. Dry-run tests also confirm no label or state writes.

props.title: The implementation stays narrow
props.deck: Native integration adds a client and an entry point, rather than another naming engine.

props.title: Use the native entry point from the checkout
props.code:
herdr-app ls
bun src/herdr-app-cli.ts rename-now \
  --tab "$TAB_ID" --config-dir "$CONFIG_DIR"
bun src/herdr-app-cli.ts watch \
  --tab "$TAB_ID" --config-dir "$CONFIG_DIR"

annotations.title: Choose a native ID
annotations.body: The target must be a local tb… ID from herdr-app, never an older w…:t… daemon ID.

annotations.title: Explicitly reclaim this tab
annotations.body: rename-now can replace a manual name. once preserves it. The configuration directory supplies your existing model selection.

annotations.title: Opt-in background behaviour
annotations.body: watch stays in this foreground process. Ctrl+C releases its lock and event subscription. It installs no login service.

props.title: Verified locally, not rolled out
props.deck: The branch is ready for review; the existing installation has not been repointed.
props.takeaway: The adapter is tested. Enabling it for daily use is a separate step.

rows.title: The final write is not atomic
rows.body: The app has no conditional rename argument. A manual edit between the last read and the command can still race. The adapter does not rewrite the whole layout to bypass this.

rows.title: Local tabs only
rows.body: Remote native spaces and native pane-label writes are deliberately unsupported. Native context does not include daemon-owned transcript excerpts.

rows.title: Existing credential scanner self-matches
rows.body: The unchanged main-branch scanner flags its own placeholder URL at byte 964. Required type, lint and contained-test gates pass; this extra scanner check is not reported as passing.

rows.title: 171 contained tests pass
rows.body: The isolated suite includes 21 native regressions. Seven separately enabled live integrations remain skipped in that run.

rows.title: Native and daemon live checks pass
rows.body: The native CLI test covers naming, late manual edits, numeric titles, failure cleanup and real watcher startup. The separate daemon manual-label regression also passes.

rows.title: Cleanup is checked, not assumed
rows.body: The scratch tab is closed, its terminal is finished, neighbouring names are unchanged and the original native selection is restored.

rows.title: No global rollout
rows.body: No plugin relink, app mod, login service or agents2 pin changed. The feature requires explicit use of the checkout's native entry point.
rows.next: Any installation or automatic startup needs a separate decision.
